samples.summary: The new live `container.style.left/top` anchoring in `mountSlidesTextBox` (isGrow branch) has no test at all; the only new editor test mocks the mount away
samples.evidence: The diff adds a third coupled surface to the #1039 fix: the live editing container is repositioned via `resizeFrameToSize` on every content-height report (text-box-editor.ts:495-506). The new `packages/slides/test/view/editor/rotated-autofit-commit.test.ts` passes `mountTextBox: makeMount(...)`, a stub whose container never reads `frame.rotation` and never sets left/top — so it cannot exercise or fail on this code. The one real-mount suite, `packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-autogrow.test.ts`, mounts only `rotation: 0` frames (lines 31, 52, 66) and asserts `container.style.height` only, never `left`/`top`. So if the live-position math were wrong (or the `isGrow` gate inverted), a rotated text box's editing surface would visibly drift/jump during editing with a fully green suite. The infrastructure to test it exists (jsdom + flushRaf + real `mountSlidesTextBox`).

samples.summary: `anchoredFramePatch`'s non-finite guard (`!Number.isFinite(next.x) || !Number.isFinite(next.y)` → fall back to the size-only patch) is never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: grep for `anchoredFramePatch`/`frame-patch` finds only src/index.tsx, docs and .agent-review notes — no test file imports the helper, and there is no `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/format-panel/frame-patch.test.ts`. The new `rotated-resize.test.tsx` only drives finite w/h values, so the NaN/Infinity degradation path the doc comment presents as the 'second belt' (and the `patch.w === undefined && patch.h === undefined` pass-through for size-less patches) is asserted nowhere. If the guard were inverted or removed, NaN coordinates could be persisted (the exact 'vanished element' hazard the comment names) with a green suite.

samples.summary: The per-element compensation claim for MULTI-element W/H commits is untested; every new test uses a single-element selection
samples.evidence: `commitFrame` now looks up each element and applies `anchoredFramePatch(el.frame, patch)` because 'each element carries its own rotation' (index.tsx:122-129), and the `el ? ... : patch` fallback covers ids missing from `selection.elements`. The new `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/format-panel/rotated-resize.test.tsx` always mounts exactly one element (`getSelection: () => [elementId]`, setup() adds a single shape), so a multi-select W/H commit over elements with DIFFERENT rotations — the case the comment justifies the refactor with — is covered by no test, nor is the id-not-found fallback. Pre-existing multi-select tests in size-position-section.test.tsx use rotation 0 only.

samples.summary: Group elements now go through `anchoredFramePatch` before `bakeGroupResize`, and no test covers a group W/H commit from the panel (rotated or not)
samples.evidence: `commitFrame` and `lockedResize` now write an anchored x/y for group elements too, then call `store.bakeGroupResize` (index.tsx:125-131, 242-253). grep for `bakeGroupResize` in packages/frontend/tests finds only yorkie-slides-equivalence.test.ts:603, which calls the store directly and never goes through the panel; the new rotated-resize.test.tsx only uses a `shape`. So the interaction between the new x/y compensation and the bake (which itself rewrites child frames) is untested; a double-applied offset on a rotated group would move the whole group with a green suite.

samples.summary: New `resizeFrameToSize` tests are placed above the mid-file `import` that provides the symbol, relying on ES import hoisting
samples.evidence: The `describe('resizeFrameToSize')` block at lines 120-164 uses `resizeFrameToSize`, but the import that adds it (line 174-179) sits below. It works via hoisting, but it makes the suite read as if the symbol were undefined and invites a future accidental reorder into a genuine runtime error rather than a test of the behavior.

verdict.reason: The new live re-anchoring in mountSlidesTextBox (text-box-editor.ts:495-506, inside the isGrow branch of onContentHeightChange) has no test. rotated-autofit-commit.test.ts uses a stub mount (makeMount, lines 22-57) whose container never reads frame.rotation nor sets left/top and drives the editor-level callback instead, so the mount code is never executed. The only real-mount grow suite, text-box-autogrow.test.ts, mounts rotation: 0 frames (lines 31, 52, 66) and asserts container.style.height only (line 44). text-box-autofit-gating.test.ts does invoke the real mount's onContentHeightChange but with a rotation: 0 frame and asserts only hook wiring/height propagation. Other real-mount suites (text-box-overflow, text-box-click-scale, text-box-initial-text) are all rotation: 0 and assert canvas overflow offsets, not the container anchor. Repo-wide searches for mountSlidesTextBox in test/spec files, container.style assertions in slides tests, non-zero rotation fixtures, #1039 references, and the frontend visual suites yielded no counterexample. Blocking: a changed, user-visible behavior (editing surface position for rotated autofit-grow boxes) with no meaningful coverage, while the two sibling surfaces of the same fix are tested.
